observations.seen: Coherent floor plan with clear zones, but it is a dollhouse of extruded boxes floating in a black void. Nothing beyond the walls.
Walls, plinths and display cases are raw boxes. The player is voxel placeholder and the two guards come from incompatible style sources.
Effectively untextured: flat albedo, no marble, no wood grain, no trim sheets, no decals.
Emissive vs. matte is the only material distinction. Gold reads as yellow plastic.
No visible roughness/metal variation and no specular response on a "marble hall" floor.
The neon emissive palette gives a decent night-heist mood, but it is unlit-looking, with no light falloff or pools on the floor.
Characters and props show no readable cast shadows. Only faint darkening at wall bases.
Flat uniform ambient with no AO in corners. Everything has the same mid-dark value.
No environment reflections anywhere. The gallery floor and glass cases reflect nothing.
Not blown out, but emissives clip to flat white (signage, ring) with no roll-off. Mids are murky.
The cyan/pink/gold/red palette is intentional and consistent, with no obvious sRGB errors.
Edges are acceptable at 1080p. Thin neon lines shimmer-prone (inferred).
Mild bloom on signage and strips only. No SSAO, DOF, vignette or grading.
Laser lines are the only effect. Vision cones are absent or broken (the stray blue quad).
None visible in any frame.
Rigid poses across frames. The voxel player shows no gait difference between SPRINT and SNEAK.
Tiny on screen, mismatched styles, and the player is a placeholder block figure.
A fixed overview works for stealth readability but is static, too far out, and wastes the bottom third.
Empty plinth and black void dominate. The subject sits high and the frame is never re-centred.
The isometric read is clear. Lack of shadows, AO and atmosphere flattens depth.
No fog, dust motes, light shafts or haze, despite neon lighting being ideal for them.
Zones are legible, but the core threat (vision cones) is invisible and the guards' facing is unclear.
Clean dark panels, but there is debug telemetry in production, redundant on-screen text buttons on desktop, and a truncated "SCORE" label.
A sensible sans pairing with tidy hierarchy. In-world signage is clipped ("TREASUR'") with a stray glyph.
No feedback states across three frames, plus the stray geometry artifact.
Canvas covers about 40% of the screen with overlapping HUD, unreadable subjects, a text-button D-pad and dead space.
Reads as an engine-integration prototype with neon trim, not a shipped showcase.
